brief: German state elections brought heavy CDU losses: AfD won 38.3% in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, roughly double its 2021 result, and Die Linke topped Berlin at 25.3%, with the CDU missing the 5% threshold in one state for the first time since WWII; this weakens Germany's political centre without an immediate national policy shift. A separate US-Denmark-Greenland agreement expands the US military presence there and, if it holds, reduces geopolitical event risk versus Trump's earlier ambition to acquire Greenland. Asian equities rallied on trade-talk optimism ahead of Thursday's Trump-Xi summit. The week ahead brings September flash PMIs Wednesday, Norges Bank/Riksbank/SNB decisions Thursday (hike probabilities priced at 62%/21%/5%), and heavy Fed speak following last week's rate hike, where updated projections showed a majority favoring further tightening even as Chair Warsh said policy is not yet meaningfully restrictive; next Friday's payrolls report is called the most important release before the October FOMC. Last week reversed course: an early energy-price spike pushed the 10yr Treasury yield above 5% for the first time since 2007 on stagflation fears, before falling oil prices, more than the Fed hike, unwound that spike; French 10yr spreads over bunds closed above 100bps for the first time since 2012.
